evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:178-191 — the SSO user-upsert path writes the IdP-supplied `info.avatar_url` straight into `profile_image_url` via `self.repo.update_user(... profile_image_url: Some(avatar.to_string()) ...)` with NO URL/scheme validation. The self-service PUT /users/me path validates the same field: routes/users.rs:354-364 explicitly runs `validate_image_or_link_url(purl)` under the 'H7' comment ('reject javascript:, data:, file: ... these end up in on the frontend') and rejects bad schemes. The SSO path bypasses that H7 guard entirely, so the two write paths into one stored, frontend-rendered field disagree on validation.

Reachability: `profile_image_url` is returned by the portal user API (routes/users.rs:107,130) and, per the H7 comments in users.rs:23 and agency_branding.rs:23, is rendered in `` on reality-web. avatar_url originates from the PM OAuth userinfo response, which is often user-editable at the IdP — so an attacker-influenced `data:`/`javascript:` avatar can be persisted through SSO that the self-service endpoint would have rejected. Defense-in-depth gap / inconsistent input validation on a stored-then-rendered field. Net-new: 0 prior reality-server signal/backlog mentions of state.rs SSO avatar handling.

Fix (backend-only, reality-server): run the IdP `avatar_url` through the same `validate_image_or_link_url` check used at routes/users.rs:357 before the state.rs:182 update_user write — on failure, skip the avatar update (keep the SSO login succeeding, since the avatar write is already best-effort `let _ =`) rather than persisting an unvalidated URL. Severity medium (missing validation on user-influenced input landing in an HTML sink, +2).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/email.rs:179-184 — SmtpPasswordResetMailer::new selects the transport as `if settings.use_tls { starttls_relay(host)? } else { builder_dangerous(host) }` and then attaches SMTP `Credentials::new(username, password)` to whichever builder is chosen. On the `else` arm, `builder_dangerous` establishes a plaintext (no STARTTLS, no certificate verification) connection, so the SMTP username+password are transmitted in cleartext and are susceptible to MITM. There is no inline comment justifying the insecure arm (the skill flags insecure transport chosen 'without a comment explaining the decision').

Mitigating context (why low, not medium): `use_tls` defaults to true (email.rs:152-154 — only `SMTP_TLS=false`/`0` disables it), so the plaintext path is opt-in and reserved for local relays; builder_dangerous is lettre's standard localhost-relay constructor. Risk is limited to deployments that explicitly set SMTP_TLS=false while also setting SMTP credentials pointed at a non-local host.

Fix (backend-only, reality-server): add an inline comment documenting that the no-TLS arm is intended only for a trusted local relay, and/or guard it so credentials are not attached (or the build fails/warns) when use_tls is false but host is not loopback/localhost. Severity low (+1).
